prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Welcome to Your Desktop Companion"]
1: ["Meet Your Virtual Desktop Buddy", "Swipe to see how your desktop pet plays, learns, and stays on screen."]
2: ["Save Your Companion to Your Account", "Link your pet now so you never lose your buddy across devices."]
3: ["Upload Pet Photos for AI Generation", "AI Photo Check Active"]
4: ["Preparing Your Pet's Desktop Home"]
5: ["Sign In to Keep Your Pet Safe", "Use your primary account so your pet state and accessories stay saved.", "Already created a pet? Sign in with the exact same account to restore it."]
6: ["Your Pet is Live on Your Screen!", "Right-click your pet anytime to hide, move, or open settings."]
7: ["Official Adoption Certificate", "Name your pet now to unlock an exclusive adoption badge!", "Starter Bonus Unlocked"]
8: ["Creating Companion...", "We will notify you on desktop as soon as your pet is ready!"]
9: ["Choose How You Want to Adopt", "Select a ready-made mascot or generate a custom pet from photos."]

verdicts.problem: Mentions free extras, bonuses, and exclusive rewards to incentivize action.
